The '''''Journal of Econometrics''''' is a monthly [[peer-reviewed]] [[academic journal]] covering [[econometrics]]. It was established in 1973.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gagliardini |first=Patrick |date=2007 |title=Challenges in the teaching of econometrics: the lesson of Pietro Balestra |url=https://www.cairn.info/revue-d-economie-politique-2007-3-page-431.htm |journal=[[Revue d'économie politique]] |volume=117 |issue=3 |pages=431–439 |doi=10.3917/rep.173.0431 |doi-access=free}}</ref> The [[editors-in-chief]] are [[Michael Jansson]] ([[University of California Berkeley]]) and [[Aureo de Paula]] ([[University College London]]).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Editorial Board |website=Journal of Econometrics |publisher=Elsevier |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/journal-of-econometrics/about/editorial-board  |access-date=2024-12-24}}</ref> According to the ''[[Journal Citation Reports]]'', the journal has a 2023 [[impact factor]] of 9.9.<ref name=WoS>{{cite book |year=2024 |chapter=Journal of Econometrics |title=2023 Journal Citation Reports |publisher=[[Clarivate]] |edition=Social Sciences |via=[[Web of Science]] |title-link=Journal Citation Reports}}</ref>

The journal covers work dealing with estimation and other [[methodology of econometrics|methodological aspects]] of the application of statistical inference to economic data, as well as papers dealing with the application of econometric techniques to [[economics]].

Unusually among journals the title of Fellow of Journal of Econometrics is offered to anyone publishing four or more articles in the Journal.<ref>Maasoumi, E. (1992). Fellow's opinion: rules of thumb and pseudo-science. Journal of Econometrics, 53(1-3), 1-4.</ref>
